body: @iocanel sounds like we should not be triggering deployment

The workaround for this for now is to put the quarkus.openshift.deploy=true as a system property rather than in the config file, so it does not take effect when you run mvn quarkus:remote-dev.

I need to think about this a bit. The remote dev mode actually run in production mode locally, to generate new production application that mirrors the one on the server. The advantage of this is that server side is always fully up to date, so if the Quarkus process is stopped and restarted (or even restarted in production mode), then the code it still up to date.
